t: Report Spam Message — Hash Set Counting
o: A message is spam if at least two of its words appear in bannedWords. In example 1 both 'hello' and 'world' match, so the answer is true; in example 2 only 'programming' matches, so false. With up to 1e5 words of length ≤ 15, hashing each word to O(length) and counting matches is easily fast enough.
k: Convert bannedWords to a set for O(1) average lookups, then count matches with early exit at 2.

a.i: Insert all banned words into a hash set, then scan message counting hits; return true as soon as the count reaches 2. Early exit means we often never read the whole message.
s: Iterate message; increment a counter for each word found in the set.
Return counter >= 2 (with early exit once it hits 2).
a.t: O(M + N) total characters — building the set and scanning the message, each word hashed in time proportional to its length.

w: This is a straight hash-set exercise; the only design decision is early exit at two matches. Pitfalls: comparing words with nested loops (O(M*N) risk), and misreading 'at least two words' as two distinct banned words — duplicates in message count separately. Follow-up: fuzzy matching (typos), which would call for a trie or edit-distance-bounded structures.
